components.css: .ds-custody { position:relative; max-width:680px; padding:28px 30px 26px; border:1px solid var(--ink, #202c28); border-radius:0; background:var(--paper, #fffdf7); color:var(--ink, #202c28); box-shadow:0 26px 70px rgba(44,52,47,.15); transform:rotate(1.25deg); } .ds-custody::before { content:''; position:absolute; inset:12px; border:1px solid var(--line, #c9cec5); pointer-events:none; } .ds-custody header,.ds-custody footer { position:relative; display:flex; align-items:center; gap:14px; font:650 10px var(--font-unbounded, sans-serif); letter-spacing:.07em; } .ds-custody header { padding-bottom:16px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--ink, #202c28); } .ds-custody header i { flex:1; border-top:3px dotted var(--line-strong, #87958e); } .ds-custody header strong { color:var(--blue, #1f56c5); } .ds-impact { position:relative; display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 56px .72fr; align-items:center; min-height:210px; } .ds-impact small { display:block; color:var(--ink-soft, #53615b); font:750 10px var(--font-public-sans, sans-serif); letter-spacing:.08em; } .ds-impact b { display:block; margin-top:16px; font:650 52px/.82 var(--font-unbounded, sans-serif); letter-spacing:-.04em; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; } .ds-impact span:last-child b { color:var(--green, #26715b); } .ds-arrow { color:var(--blue, #1f56c5); font-size:28px; } .ds-custody footer { justify-content:space-between; padding-top:22px; border-top:1px solid var(--line, #c9cec5); color:var(--ink-soft, #53615b); } .ds-custody footer strong { padding:9px 12px; border:2px solid var(--red, #c13d30); color:var(--red, #c13d30); transform:rotate(-4deg); } .ds-custody:hover { transform:rotate(.5deg); } .ds-custody:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--focus, #1f56c5); outline-offset:3px; }

components.css: .ds-ledger { position:relative; max-width:560px; padding:34px; border-radius:0; background:var(--paper, #fffdf7); color:var(--ink, #202c28); box-shadow:0 28px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.22); transform:rotate(1deg); } .ds-entry { display:block; padding-bottom:22px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--ink, #202c28); font:700 10px var(--font-unbounded, sans-serif); letter-spacing:.08em; } .ds-verified { position:absolute; right:30px; top:28px; padding:9px; border:2px solid var(--green, #26715b); color:var(--green, #26715b); font:700 10px var(--font-unbounded, sans-serif); transform:rotate(5deg); } .ds-ledger dl { margin:24px 0; } .ds-ledger dl div { display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1.4fr; gap:20px; padding:13px 0; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line, #c9cec5); font:13px var(--font-public-sans, sans-serif); } .ds-ledger dt { color:var(--ink-soft, #53615b); } .ds-ledger dd { margin:0; font-weight:750; text-align:right; } .ds-ledger .ds-pass { color:var(--green, #26715b); } .ds-ledger .ds-fail { color:var(--red, #c13d30); } .ds-ledger footer { color:var(--ink-soft, #53615b); font:11px ui-monospace, monospace; } .ds-ledger:hover { transform:rotate(.4deg); } .ds-ledger:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--focus, #1f56c5); outline-offset:3px; }

narrative.overview:
Provenance Firewall presents security as physical, reviewable evidence. Mineral paper, custody-blue annotations, evidence-yellow bands, failure-red stamps, perforations, signed ledger sheets, and slight document rotations make source authority visible without falling into either cyberpunk theater or a generic SaaS security dashboard.

The system alternates between persuasive evidence artifacts and a dense operating surface. The first mode uses oversized numbers, split statements, and documents that appear handled and stamped; the second uses strict tables, inspectors, tabs, and explicit state labels. Square construction, dark rules, and restrained shadows keep both modes part of the same evidentiary world.

The primary implementation uses no shipping raster imagery. Its seal and paper details are CSS, and its interface symbols are inline SVG icons. Any future shipping raster must carry recorded provenance; an unreviewed or undocumented asset is unfinished.
keyCharacteristics: Mineral-paper light surfaces with dark, ledger-like rules.
Custody blue for traced authority and interactive emphasis.
Evidence yellow for proof and attention, failure red for blocked or unsafe outcomes, and verified green for successful controls.
Square forms, stamps, perforations, signed sheets, and tabular evidence instead of rounded dashboard cards.
Unbounded for declarative statements and labels; Public Sans for explanatory and operating text.
A deliberate shift from 50,000 exposed records to zero, then from explanation into a live control plane.

rules.name: The Verdict Color Rule
rules.body: Red and green communicate explicit security outcomes; pair them with labels, icons, or numbers so color never carries the verdict alone.

rules.name: The Evidence Yellow Rule
rules.body: Yellow marks proof or a deliberate call to inspect it. Do not use it as a generic cheerful accent.

rules.name: The Paper Majority Rule
rules.body: Mineral ground and ledger paper remain the visual majority; saturated colors work because they are bounded and evidentiary.

rules.name: The Institutional Label Rule
rules.body: Use uppercase Unbounded sparingly for metadata and state, never for paragraphs.

rules.name: The Number Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Consequential totals are large, tightly set, and tabular; 50,000 and zero must scan before their explanation.

rules.name: The Artifact-to-Console Rule
rules.body: Persuasive sections may rotate and breathe; operating sections align to strict columns and square borders.

rules.name: The Loose-Paper Rule
rules.body: Shadows and rotation belong to evidence that reads as a handled sheet, never to routine dashboard containers.

rules.name: The No Soft Card Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce rounded, floating SaaS cards; divide information with paper fields, rules, columns, and ledger rows.

dos: Do make source, authority, requirement, decision, and signature visible as a chain of evidence.
Do use square paper artifacts, strict rules, stamps, perforations, and ledger rows to organize proof.
Do reserve custody blue for action and trace, evidence yellow for proof, and verdict colors for explicit outcomes.
Do keep the 50,000-to-zero result visually dominant and pair every result color with text or iconography.
Do preserve strict operating columns and horizontal scrolling when evidence cannot collapse safely.
Do attach provenance to every raster that is approved for shipping; prefer CSS or inline SVG when an asset does not need to be rasterized.
donts: Don't turn the interface into a generic rounded-card SaaS security dashboard.
Don't use dark cyberpunk surfaces, neon glows, glass cards, or decorative threat-map imagery.
Don't add shadows or rotation to ordinary controls, tabs, tables, or console containers.
Don't use red and green without a written verdict, state label, number, or icon.
Don't fabricate customer imagery, production evidence, testimonials, or security claims.
Don't ship an unreviewed, undocumented, or provenance-free raster asset.
